kicker_candidates: Specialty chemicals processor eyes NSE SME listing

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals buys mineral raw materials, processes them into specialty chemicals, and sells them to industrial customers. Its product categories are Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM).

The company has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network. This is a central feature of its business model.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of the last three full financial years (FY2015, FY2016, FY2017).
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, and has achieved cumulative exports of ₹10.68 crore (1,068.18 lakh) over five years.

The DRHP lists six competitive strengths: a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support from the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: The DRHP provides restated financials for six periods: the six months ended 30 September 2017, and each full fiscal year from FY2013 to FY2017. All figures are in ₹ lakh.

The company reported losses in FY2013 (PAT ₹-27.40 lakh) and FY2014 (PAT ₹-12.17 lakh), but turned profitable from FY2015 onwards. PAT was ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, and ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017. For the six months ended Sep 2017, PAT was ₹132.75 lakh.

Operating cash flow was positive ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, and ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016. It turned sharply negative at ₹-349.75 lakh in FY2017. For the six-month period ended Sep 2017, it was ₹124.86 lakh.
Total assets grew from ₹2,679.38 lakh in FY2013 to ₹3,424.96 lakh by Sep 2017, indicating expansion. However, debt levels are not explicitly disclosed in the digest excerpts.
Basic earnings per share (EPS) was negative in FY2013 (₹-0.45) and FY2014 (₹-0.20), but turned positive: ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for six months ended Sep 2017.

beats.beat: The company has four promoters: three individuals — Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, and Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh — and the corporate entity 20 Microns Limited.
Collectively, the promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds the remaining 0.24%.

The company has entered into related party transactions in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended Sep 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18. These are detailed in the financial statements.

The DRHP notes past instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, which were later regularized with additional fees. It also states that the company has not yet obtained all required licenses for one of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia).
The company and its promoters are parties to certain legal proceedings. The filing does not quantify the potential financial impact.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1,000 billion in FY2017, growing at 10-12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017. CRISIL Research forecasts 12-14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented, with small and medium enterprises (SMEs) holding 70-75% market share. Only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants on product development.

Demand is driven by rising GDP, urbanization, improved consumption standards, and government initiatives. FDI up to 100% is allowed, and a Draft National Chemical Policy aims to boost the chemical sector's share of GDP.

The filing acknowledges headwinds: changes in environmental regulations, GST implementation from July 2017, and stricter European REACH rules affecting exports. China's tighter environmental norms are seen as an opportunity for Indian players.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — a range that includes functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals and hard minerals. It is a subsidiary of 20 Microns Limited and relies on its corporate promoter for sales and marketing.

The company is raising money through a fresh issue of equity shares to be listed on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). The proceeds will fund a new manufacturing facility in Vadodara, Gujarat, and general corporate purposes.
Promoters hold 99.76% of the pre-issue equity. The issue will dilute their holding and create a public market for the stock.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does, and what the IPO is about.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale). The specific number of shares and price band are not disclosed in the DRHP.

Proceeds will be used for: (1) capital expenditure on a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (2) general corporate purposes; and (3) creating a public market for the company's shares by listing on NSE EMERGE.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited. The registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

beats.beat: Dependence on corporate promoter: The company has no independent sales network; it relies on 20 Microns Limited to market and sell its products. Termination or disruption of this arrangement would severely hurt revenue.

No long-term contracts: The company does not have long-term or definitive agreements with customers or raw material suppliers. It operates on purchase orders and spot purchases, exposing it to volume and price volatility.

Negative operating cash flow in FY2017: Operating cash flow swung from ₹802.59 lakh positive in FY2016 to ₹-349.75 lakh in FY2017. Sustained negative cash flows could constrain growth and require additional financing.

Missing regulatory licenses: The company has not yet obtained certain statutory and regulatory approvals for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia. This could lead to penalties or operational disruption.

Related party transactions: The company has a history of related party transactions and may continue them. There is no assurance that these will not have an adverse effect on financial condition, given the high promoter ownership concentration.
